raus-.et: Contraction of heraus- or from raus.

rauschig.et:
Rausch (“intoxication”) + -ig.
In the 1830s, Gregor Dankovszky compared the term to Hungarian részeg (“drunk”), but the similarity must be coincidental, because Gábor Zaicz takes részeg to be of Ugric or Uralic origin.

rausbringen.et: Shortening of herausbringen (“to bring out; release”). Equivalent to raus- + bringen.

rauscharm.et: From Rauschen (gerund of rauschen (“to rustle”)) + -arm (“low in”, literally “poor”). The suffix -arm is added to nominals; nevertheless the gerund behaves like a normal infinitive dropping the suffix -en. Derivation from Rausch is semantically ruled out.
